readings.title: The Covenant of the Pieces
readings.subtitle: Abram's Vision and the Prophecy of Sojourning
readings.text: [Genesis 15:1] After these events the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Aḇram in a vision, saying, <dq>Do not be afraid, Aḇram. <dn>I</dn> am your shield, your reward is exceedingly great.</dq> [2] And Aḇram said, “Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, what would <dn>You</dn> give me, seeing I go childless, and the heir of my house is Eli‛ezer of Dammeseq?” [3] And Aḇram said, “See, <dn>You</dn> have given me no seed, and see, one born in my house is my heir!” [4] And see, the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to him, saying, <dq>This one is not your heir, but he who comes from your own body is your heir.</dq> [5] And <dn>He</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> him outside and said, <dq>Look now toward the heavens, and count the stars if you are able to count them.</dq> And <dn>He</dn> said to him, <dq>So are your seed.</dq> [6] And he believed in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> reckoned it to him for righteousness. [7] And <dn>He</dn> said to him, <dq><dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who brought you out of Ur-kasdim, to give you <dn>את</dn> this land to inherit it.</dq> [8] And he said, “Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, whereby do I know that I possess it?” [9] And <dn>He</dn> said to him, <dq>Bring <dn>Me</dn> a three-year-old heifer, and a three-year-old female goat, and a three-year-old ram, and a turtledove, and a young pigeon.</dq> [10] And he took <dn>את</dn> all these to <dn>Him</dn> and cut <dn>את</dn> them in the middle, and placed each half opposite the other, but he did not cut <dn>את</dn> the birds. [11] And the birds of prey came down on the carcasses, and Aḇram drove them away. [12] And it came to be, when the sun was going down, and a deep sleep fell upon Aḇram, that see, a frightening great darkness fell upon him. [13] And <dn>He</dn> said to Aḇram, <dq>Know for certain that your seed are to be sojourners in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them, and they shall afflict <dn>את</dn> them four hundred years.</dq> [14] <dq>But <dn>את</dn> the nation whom they serve <dn>I</dn> am going to judge, and afterward let them come out with great possessions.</dq> [15] <dq>Now as for you, you are to go to your fathers in peace, you are to be buried at a good old age.</dq> [16] <dq>Then, in the fourth generation they shall return here, for the crookedness of the Amorites is not yet complete.</dq> [17] And it came to be, when the sun went down and it was dark, that see, a smoking oven and a burning torch passing between those pieces. [18] On the same day <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made a covenant with <dn>את</dn> Aḇram, saying, <dq><dn>I</dn> have given <dn>את</dn> this land to your seed, from the river of Mitsrayim to the great river, the River Euphrates,</dq> [19] <dq>with <dn>את</dn> the Qěynite, and <dn>את</dn> the Qenizzite, and <dn>את</dn> the Qaḏmonite,</dq> [20] <dq>and <dn>את</dn> the Ḥittite, and <dn>את</dn> the Perizzite, and <dn>את</dn> the Repha’im,</dq> [21] <dq>and <dn>את</dn> the Amorite, and <dn>את</dn> the Kena‛anite, and <dn>את</dn> the Girgashite, and <dn>את</dn> the Yeḇusite.</dq>

readings.title: The Birth of Ishmael
readings.subtitle: Hagar's Flight and the Messenger of YeHoVaH
readings.text: [Genesis 16:1] And Sarai, Aḇram’s wife, had borne him no child. And she had a Mitsrian female servant whose name was Haḡar. [2] And Sarai said to Aḇram, “See, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has kept me from bearing children. Please, go in to my female servant. It might be that I am built up by her.” And Aḇram listened to the voice of Sarai. [3] And Sarai, Aḇram’s wife, took <dn>את</dn> Haḡar her female servant, the Mitsrian, and gave her to her husband Aḇram to be his wife, after Aḇram had dwelt ten years in the land of Kena‛an. [4] And he went in to Haḡar, and she conceived. And when she saw that she had conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes. [5] And Sarai said to Aḇram, “My wrong be upon you! I gave my female servant into your bosom. And when she saw that she had conceived, I was despised in her eyes. Let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> judge between you and me.” [6] And Aḇram said to Sarai, “See, your female servant is in your hand, do to her what is good in your eyes.” And Sarai treated her harshly, and she fled from her presence. [7] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> found her by a spring of water in the wilderness, by the spring on the way to Shur, [8] and <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>Haḡar, Sarai’s female servant, where have you come from, and where are you going?</dq> And she said, “I am fleeing from the presence of Sarai, my mistress.” [9] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to her, <dq>Return to your mistress, and humble yourself under her hand.</dq> [10] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to her, <dq><dn>I</dn> am going to increase your seed greatly, too numerous to be counted.</dq> [11] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to her, <dq>See, you are conceiving and bearing a son, and shall call his name Yishma‛ěl, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has heard your affliction.</dq> [12] <dq>And he is to be a wild man, his hand against every one and every one’s hand against him, and dwell over against all his brothers.</dq> [13] And she called the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who spoke to her, “<dn>You</dn> are the <dn>Ěl</dn> who sees,” for she said, “Even here have I seen after <dn>Him</dn> who sees me?” [14] That is why the well was called Be’ěr Laḥai Ro’i, see, it is between Qaḏěsh and Bereḏ. [15] And Haḡar bore Aḇram a son, and Aḇram called the name of his son, whom Haḡar bore, Yishma‛ěl. [16] And Aḇram was eighty-six years old when Haḡar bore Yishma‛ěl to Aḇram.

readings.title: The Sign of Circumcision
readings.subtitle: The Renaming of Abram and Sarai
readings.text: [Genesis 17:1] And it came to be when Aḇram was ninety-nine years old, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to Aḇram and said to him, <dq><dn>I</dn> am <dn>Ěl</dn> Shaddai – walk before <dn>Me</dn> and be perfect.</dq> [2] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> give <dn>My</dn> covenant between <dn>Me</dn> and you, and shall greatly increase you.</dq> [3] And Aḇram fell on his face, and <dn>Elohim</dn> spoke with him, saying, [4] <dq>As for <dn>Me</dn>, look, <dn>My</dn> covenant is with you, and you shall become a father of many nations.</dq> [5] <dq>And no longer is <dn>את</dn> your name called Aḇram, but your name shall be Aḇraham, because <dn>I</dn> shall make you a father of many nations.</dq> [6] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall make you exceedingly fruitful, and make nations of you, and sovereigns shall come from you.</dq> [7] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant between <dn>Me</dn> and you and your seed after you in their generations, for an everlasting covenant, to be <dn>Elohim</dn> to you and your seed after you.</dq> [8] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall give to you and your seed after you <dn>את</dn> the land of your sojournings, <dn>את</dn> all the land of Kena‛an, as an everlasting possession. And <dn>I</dn> shall be their <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [9] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to Aḇraham, <dq>As for you, guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant, you and your seed after you throughout their generations.</dq> [10] <dq>This is <dn>My</dn> covenant which you guard between <dn>Me</dn> and you, and your seed after you: Every male child among you is to be circumcised.</dq> [11] <dq>And you shall circumcise <dn>את</dn> the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall become a sign of the covenant between <dn>Me</dn> and you.</dq> [12] <dq>And a son of eight days is circumcised by you, every male child in your generations, he who is born in your house or bought with silver from any foreigner who is not of your seed.</dq> [13] <dq>He who is born in your house, and he who is bought with your silver, has to be circumcised. So shall <dn>My</dn> covenant be in your flesh, for an everlasting covenant.</dq> [14] <dq>And an uncircumcised male child, who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin, his life shall be cut off from his people – he has broken <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant.</dq> [15] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to Aḇraham, <dq>As for Sarai your wife, do not call <dn>את</dn> her name Sarai, for Sarah is her name.</dq> [16] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall bless <dn>את</dn> her and also give you a son by her. And <dn>I</dn> shall bless her, and she shall become nations – sovereigns of peoples are to be from her.</dq> [17] And Aḇraham fell on his face and laughed, and said in his heart, “Is a child born to a man who is a hundred years old? Or is Sarah, who is ninety years old, to bear a child?” [18] And Aḇraham said to <dn>Elohim</dn>, “Oh, let Yishma‛ěl live before <dn>You</dn>!” [19] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said, <dq>No, Sarah your wife is truly bearing a son to you, and you shall call <dn>את</dn> his name Yitsḥaq. And <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant with <dn>את</dn> him for an everlasting covenant, and with his seed after him.</dq> [20] <dq>And as for Yishma‛ěl, <dn>I</dn> have heard you. See, <dn>I</dn> shall bless <dn>את</dn> him, and shall make him fruitful, and greatly increase <dn>את</dn> him. He is to bring forth twelve princes, and <dn>I</dn> shall make him a great nation.</dq> [21] <dq>But <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant <dn>I</dn> establish with Yitsḥaq, whom Sarah is to bear to you at this appointed time next year.</dq> [22] And when <dn>He</dn> had ended speaking with him, <dn>Elohim</dn> went up from Aḇraham. [23] And Aḇraham took <dn>את</dn> Yishma‛ěl his son, and <dn>את</dn> all those born in his house and <dn>את</dn> all those bought with his silver, every male among the men of Aḇraham’s house, and circumcised <dn>את</dn> the flesh of their foreskins that same day, as <dn>Elohim</dn> told him. [24] And Aḇraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin. [25] And Yishma‛ěl his son was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin. [26] Aḇraham and his son Yishma‛ěl were circumcised that same day. [27] And all the men of his house, born in the house or bought with silver from a foreigner, were circumcised with him.
